events.content: Done. `app/ProductGallery.tsx` now renders each product's image at 300x200 using `product.imageUrl`. **Pattern followed:** `app/page.tsx:10-16` uses the `next/image` `Image` component with explicit `src`/`alt`/`width`/`height` (and is labeled "Good example" in a comment), so I used the same component and prop shape rather than a raw ``. Two deliberate deviations from the hero: - **`alt={product.name}`** — the hero hardcodes its alt text; here it comes from the product data so each image gets a distinct description. - **No `priority`** — the hero sets it because it's the above-the-fold LCP element. Gallery thumbnails should stay lazy-loaded, which is `next/image`'s default; copying `priority` to all three would defeat the point of the hero's own hint. **Verified:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, and `npm run build` compiles and prerenders all routes successfully. Two things worth flagging, both pre-existing and left alone: - **The image files don't exist.** There's no `public/` directory, so `/product-1.jpg` (and `/hero-image.jpg`, already referenced on the homepage) will 404 at runtime. The build passes because `next/image` resolves local paths at request time, not build time. You'll need to add `public/product-{1,2,3}.jpg` to actually see images. - **`next build` rewrites `tsconfig.json`** — it reformats the arrays and adds `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`. I reverted that plus the generated `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` to keep the diff to just the component, but it will come back the next time anyone builds. Adding `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` to `.gitignore` would stop the artifacts from showing up as untracked noise; say the word and I'll do it. The `package.json` modification and untracked `package-lock.json` were already in the working tree before I started; I didn't touch them.
